parts.title: Part A
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y elige la respuesta que mejor responde a la pregunta. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Are you going to apply for the grant?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I might as well. The deadline is not until June.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «I might as well» = no tengo nada que perder, probablemente lo haga.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: How is the new supervisor?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The jury is still out.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She has not formed an opinion yet.
questions.explanation: «The jury is still out» = todavía no hay veredicto, aún no lo tengo claro.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did the printer work in the end?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: After three hours, sort of.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
questions.explanation: «Sort of» = más o menos, a medias.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Should I take the eight o'clock train?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: If I were you, I would take the earlier one.

questions.stem: What does the woman advise?
questions.explanation: «If I were you» introduce un consejo claro.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do you think the proposal will pass?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I would not bet on it.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «I would not bet on it» expresa duda, no apuestas literales.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The seminar starts at four, right?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: They moved it back an hour.

questions.stem: When does the seminar start?
questions.explanation: «Move back» retrasa la hora: de cuatro a cinco.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Have you read the whole book?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I have barely scratched the surface.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Scratch the surface» = quedarse en lo superficial, apenas empezar.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you want to split the taxi?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I am walking, but thanks anyway.

questions.stem: What will the woman do?
questions.explanation: Rechaza cortésmente y dice lo que hará.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How did the interview go?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I would rather not talk about it.

questions.stem: What can be inferred?
options: He has not had it yet.
questions.explanation: Evitar el tema sugiere que no fue bien.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The department is cutting the budget again.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Here we go again.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Here we go again» = otra vez lo mismo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Can you finish it by Thursday?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It will be tight, but yes.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He can finish it with difficulty.
questions.explanation: «Tight» = justo de tiempo, pero acepta.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is the professor strict about attendance?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Let us just say I would not skip.

questions.stem: What does the woman imply?
questions.explanation: Respuesta indirecta que confirma la sospecha.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did you hear back about the apartment?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Not a word.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Not a word» = ninguna respuesta.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: This assignment is due tomorrow.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Since when?

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She is surprised by the deadline.
questions.explanation: «Since when?» dicho así expresa sorpresa, no una pregunta literal de fecha.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Are you two working together on this?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: We see things very differently.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
questions.explanation: Forma educada de decir que no están de acuerdo.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you need help carrying those?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I have got it, thanks.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «I have got it» = ya me apaño.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The results came out today.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: And?

questions.stem: What does the man want?
options: To know what the results were.
questions.explanation: «And?» pide que siga contando.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is it worth taking the advanced course?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: It depends on what you want to do afterwards.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: The answer depends on his plans.
questions.explanation: No se moja: la respuesta depende de sus objetivos.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I have to present tomorrow and nothing is ready.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: You will pull it off. You always do.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He will do it for her.
questions.explanation: «Pull it off» = sacarlo adelante.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did they accept your paper?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: With revisions.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: It was accepted but must be changed.
questions.explanation: «With revisions» = aceptado con cambios.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Was the lecture useful?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I got more out of the reading, honestly.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
questions.explanation: «Get more out of» = sacar más provecho.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you mind if I open the window?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Not at all.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Not at all» responde a «do you mind» dando permiso.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The conference is in Berlin this year.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: There goes my travel budget.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «There goes my budget» = adiós a mi presupuesto.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Should we start without her?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Give her five more minutes.

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest?
questions.explanation: Pide esperar cinco minutos más.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How is the thesis coming along?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Slowly but surely.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Slowly but surely» = despacio pero avanzando.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Everyone says the exam is impossible.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do not let that get to you.

questions.stem: What does the woman advise?
options: Not to be affected by it.
questions.explanation: «Get to you» = afectarte.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did you find the reference?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It was right under my nose.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Right under my nose» = lo tenía delante.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are you free this weekend?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I am swamped until Monday.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Swamped» = desbordado de trabajo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The article says the effect is permanent.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I would take that with a grain of salt.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Take with a grain of salt» = no tragárselo del todo.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you want to review my draft?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Send it over. I have some time this evening.

questions.stem: What will the woman do?
questions.explanation: «Send it over» acepta y da el momento.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I wanted to ask about the internship credit. My placement is only ten hours a week.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Ten hours will give you two credits rather than four. The four-credit option requires twenty.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Is there any way to combine two placements?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: There is, but both have to be approved before you start, and one of yours began in September.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: So that one cannot count retroactively.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Not for credit, no. It can still go on your record as experience, which matters for references.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I need four credits to graduate on schedule.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Then your options are to increase the hours at your current placement, or to take a two-credit seminar alongside it.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Which do students usually choose?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: The seminar, because employers rarely agree to double the hours halfway through.

questions.stem: Why is the student speaking to the coordinator?
questions.explanation: Lo plantea en la primera intervención.

questions.stem: How many hours are needed for four credits?
questions.explanation: «The four-credit option requires twenty».

questions.stem: Why can the September placement not count for credit?
options: It was not approved before it began.
questions.explanation: Ambas colocaciones deben aprobarse antes de empezar.

questions.stem: What does the coordinator say most students choose?
questions.explanation: Porque los empleadores casi nunca aceptan doblar las horas a mitad.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The archive said the letters are too fragile to photocopy.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did they offer to scan them?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: They did, but the queue is eight weeks and my chapter is due in five.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You could transcribe them on site. Tedious, but it is allowed.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Two hundred letters by hand. That is a week of work at least.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do you need all two hundred, though?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Probably not. About forty are from the period I am covering.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Then transcribe those forty and request the scans for the rest. The scans arrive after your deadline but before the thesis is bound.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: That would work. I had been treating it as all or nothing.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Most archive problems are solved by narrowing the question, not by finding a faster machine.

questions.stem: What is the man's problem?
options: He cannot copy the letters in time.
questions.explanation: No se pueden fotocopiar y el escaneo tarda ocho semanas.

questions.stem: How long is the scanning queue?
questions.explanation: Dato explícito.

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest he do first?
options: Transcribe only the relevant forty letters.
questions.explanation: Transcribir las cuarenta del periodo y pedir el escaneo del resto.

questions.stem: What general point does the woman make at the end?
options: Narrowing the question often solves the problem.
questions.explanation: Última intervención, explícita.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Today I want to talk about why the metric system took so long to be adopted in some countries, and what that tells us about standards in general.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The usual explanation is national pride, and that plays a part, but it is not the main obstacle.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The main obstacle is that a unit of measurement is not just a number. It is embedded in tools, in contracts, in the size of a brick and the width of a road.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Changing the unit means changing all of those at once, or living with two systems during the transition, which is when accidents happen.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The most expensive documented example is a spacecraft lost in 1999 because one team worked in metric units and another did not.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The lesson is not that one system is better. It is that the cost of a standard lies almost entirely in the switch, not in the standard itself.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?
options: Why adopting a new standard is difficult.
questions.explanation: Es el hilo de toda la charla.

questions.stem: According to the professor, what is the main obstacle?
options: The cost of new instruments only.
Units are embedded in tools and contracts.
questions.explanation: Lo dice explícitamente tras descartar el orgullo nacional.

questions.stem: When do accidents happen, according to the talk?
options: During the period when two systems coexist.
questions.explanation: «living with two systems during the transition, which is when accidents happen».

questions.stem: What is the professor's conclusion?
options: The cost lies in switching, not in the standard.
questions.explanation: Última frase de la charla.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Curator
script.text: Welcome. This gallery holds objects that were made to be used, not displayed, and that changes how we should look at them.

script.speaker: Curator
script.text: The wear on a handle tells you more about daily life than the decoration does.

script.speaker: Curator
script.text: Take the grinding stones in the first case. They are worn on one side only, which tells us the user was right-handed and worked seated.

script.speaker: Curator
script.text: We can even estimate the number of hours, because the rate of wear on that stone type has been measured experimentally.

script.speaker: Curator
script.text: One of these shows roughly three thousand hours of use. That is a person's working life in a single object.

script.speaker: Curator
script.text: Please do not touch the cases. The oils on our hands are, ironically, the fastest way to destroy an object that survived four thousand years of use.

questions.stem: What does the curator say the wear on objects reveals?
questions.explanation: Segunda intervención.

questions.stem: What can be deduced from the grinding stones?
options: The user was right-handed and seated.
questions.explanation: Desgaste en un solo lado.

questions.stem: How can hours of use be estimated?
options: By the size of the stone.
The wear rate has been measured experimentally.
questions.explanation: Lo explica antes de dar la cifra.

questions.stem: Why does the curator ask visitors not to touch?
options: Oils from hands damage the objects quickly.
questions.explanation: Último punto de la charla.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 3
parts.instructions: Escucha el anuncio y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: This is an announcement for students registered in the winter field course.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Departure has been moved from Friday morning to Thursday evening because of the forecast.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The bus will leave from the north gate at seven, not from the usual stop.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Bring your own sleeping bag. The ones provided last year are no longer available.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: If you cannot travel a day earlier, contact the department office before Tuesday and a place will be held for you on the Friday minibus.

questions.stem: Why has the departure been changed?
questions.explanation: Explícito en la segunda frase.

questions.stem: Where will the bus leave from?
questions.explanation: Del portón norte, no de la parada habitual.

questions.stem: What must students bring this year?
questions.explanation: Los sacos ya no se prestan.

questions.stem: What should students do if they cannot leave Thursday?
questions.explanation: Se les guarda plaza en el minibús del viernes.

parts.title: Structure
parts.instructions: Elige la palabra o frase que completa correctamente la oración.

questions.stem: A number of volunteers ______ already withdrawn from the study.
questions.explanation: «A number of» va en plural. Ojo: «the number of» va en singular.

questions.stem: The technique, ______ in the 1970s, is still used today.
questions.explanation: Participio pasado reducido: «which was developed» → «developed». Las otras dejan dos verbos principales.

questions.stem: Seldom ______ a species adapt so quickly to a new environment.
questions.explanation: Inversión tras «seldom»: does + sujeto + verbo base.

questions.stem: It is essential that every sample ______ labelled before storage.
questions.explanation: Subjuntivo tras «it is essential that»: forma base «be».

questions.stem: ______ the funding been approved earlier, the project would have finished on time.
questions.explanation: Condicional invertido: «Had the funding been approved» = «If the funding had been approved».

questions.stem: The two theories differ less in their conclusions than ______.
questions.explanation: Estructura paralela: «in their conclusions» exige «in their methods».

questions.stem: Not only ______ the results surprising, but they also contradicted earlier work.
questions.explanation: Tras «not only» al principio, el verbo se adelanta: «were the results».

questions.stem: ______ makes the discovery remarkable is its simplicity.
questions.explanation: Frase escindida con «what»: «What makes X remarkable is Y».

questions.stem: The material expands ______ it is heated above sixty degrees.
questions.explanation: «Whenever» introduce la condición temporal. Las otras no encajan gramatical o semánticamente.

questions.stem: Neither the samples nor the equipment ______ available at the time.
questions.explanation: Con «neither... nor» el verbo concuerda con el sujeto más cercano: «the equipment», singular.

questions.stem: The report is due Friday, ______ means we have two days.
questions.explanation: «Which» se refiere a toda la oración anterior. «That» no puede usarse en relativas explicativas.

questions.stem: Of all the proposals submitted, hers was ______.
questions.explanation: Con más de dos elementos se usa superlativo con artículo.

questions.stem: The professor objected to ______ without consultation.
questions.explanation: «Object to» va seguido de gerundio, no de infinitivo.

questions.stem: So dense ______ the fog that the flight was cancelled.
questions.explanation: Inversión tras «so + adjetivo» al principio: «So dense was the fog that...».

questions.stem: Little ______ about the effects of the drug when it was first approved.
questions.explanation: «Little» al principio es negativo y fuerza la inversión con pasiva: «was known».

parts.title: Written Expression
parts.instructions: Señala el fragmento subrayado que NO es correcto.

questions.stem: (A) The evidence suggests (B) that the two events (C) is related, (D) though not causally.
questions.explanation: «Events» es plural: are related.

questions.stem: (A) Although the theory is old, (B) it explains (C) the data (D) more good than any alternative.
questions.explanation: «More good» no existe: better.

questions.stem: (A) The laboratory, (B) together with its archives, (C) were destroyed (D) in the fire.
questions.explanation: «Together with» no cambia el sujeto: was destroyed.

questions.stem: (A) She has worked here (B) for 2019, (C) and she plans (D) to stay another year.
questions.explanation: Con un punto en el tiempo va «since»: since 2019.

questions.stem: (A) The instrument measures (B) temperature, (C) pressure and (D) how humid it is.
questions.explanation: Estructura paralela rota: los tres deben ser sustantivos. Debería ser «humidity».

questions.stem: (A) Every one of the (B) participants (C) were asked (D) to sign the form.
questions.explanation: «Every one of» va en singular: was asked.

questions.stem: (A) The findings, (B) which they were published last year, (C) have been widely (D) cited since then.
options: which they were published last year
questions.explanation: El «they» sobra: «which were published».

questions.stem: (A) He is interested (B) to learn (C) more about (D) the process.
questions.explanation: «Interested in learning». Tras «interested in» va gerundio.

questions.stem: (A) The committee will meet (B) on next Tuesday (C) to discuss (D) the proposal.
questions.explanation: Con «next» no se usa preposición: next Tuesday.

questions.stem: (A) By 1990 the population (B) has doubled, (C) and the city (D) had run out of space.
questions.explanation: «By 1990» exige pasado perfecto: had doubled.

questions.stem: (A) The results were (B) so surprising (C) that nobody (D) hardly believed them.
questions.explanation: Doble negación: «nobody» y «hardly» juntos. Debería ser «that hardly anybody believed them».

questions.stem: (A) There is (B) little evidences (C) that the method (D) works at scale.
questions.explanation: «Evidence» es incontable: little evidence, sin -s.

questions.stem: (A) The author explains (B) clear that (C) the two processes (D) are unrelated.
questions.explanation: Adverbio: explains clearly.

questions.stem: (A) Despite the delay, (B) the team managed (C) finishing the analysis (D) before the deadline.
questions.explanation: «Manage» va con infinitivo: managed to finish.

questions.stem: (A) The samples that (B) we collected (C) it were stored (D) at low temperature.
questions.explanation: El «it» sobra y además no concuerda: «were stored».

questions.stem: (A) Most of researchers (B) in the field (C) accept the (D) revised model.
questions.explanation: «Most researchers» o «most of the researchers». «Most of researchers» no es correcto.

questions.stem: (A) The technique allows (B) to measure (C) very small (D) changes in mass.
questions.explanation: «Allow» necesita objeto antes del infinitivo: «allows us to measure» o «allows the measurement of».

questions.stem: (A) Neither of the two hypotheses (B) explain (C) why the effect (D) disappears at altitude.
questions.explanation: «Neither of» va en singular: explains.

questions.stem: (A) The professor suggested (B) that the student (C) repeats the experiment (D) under new conditions.
questions.explanation: Subjuntivo tras «suggest»: repeat, sin -s.

questions.stem: (A) The building is (B) three times (C) more tall than (D) the one beside it.
questions.explanation: Adjetivo corto: taller than, no «more tall».

questions.stem: (A) Scientists have (B) been studying the phenomenon (C) since (D) more than forty years.
questions.explanation: Con duración va «for»: for more than forty years.

questions.stem: (A) The data was collected (B) carefully, (C) analysed thoroughly and (D) with accurate presentation.
questions.explanation: Paralelismo roto: debería ser «presented accurately».

questions.stem: (A) He asked me (B) that where (C) the laboratory (D) was located.
questions.explanation: En estilo indirecto con pregunta no se usa «that»: «asked me where».

questions.stem: (A) The theory was (B) widely accepted until (C) new evidence (D) had emerged in 2015.
questions.explanation: Con una fecha concreta va pasado simple: emerged in 2015.

questions.stem: (A) The mineral is (B) composed by (C) three elements (D) in equal proportions.
questions.explanation: «Composed of», no «composed by».

parts.title: Texto 1
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Sourdough bread depends on a partnership between two kinds of organism that would ordinarily compete. Wild yeasts consume the simple sugars in flour and release carbon dioxide, which raises the dough. Lactic acid bacteria consume other sugars that the yeasts cannot use, and produce acids that give the bread its characteristic sourness.

What makes the arrangement stable is that each organism creates conditions the other tolerates better than its rivals do. The acids produced by the bacteria lower the pH to a level that most competing microbes cannot survive, but the particular yeasts involved can. In return, the yeasts release compounds that the bacteria use for growth.

A mature starter is therefore not a single culture but an ecosystem, and like any ecosystem it reflects its surroundings. Starters maintained in different kitchens diverge within weeks, acquiring organisms from the flour, the air and the hands of the baker.

This has been used to explain why bakers report that a starter carried from one city to another eventually changes character. Controlled studies support the observation but attribute it mainly to flour rather than to location, which suggests that the romance of local air has been somewhat overstated.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Sourdough depends on a stable partnership between yeasts and bacteria.
Sourdough is healthier than other bread.
Bakers should not move starters between cities.
Wild yeasts are difficult to cultivate.
questions.explanation: El texto describe la asociación y por qué es estable.

questions.stem: What do the yeasts produce?
questions.explanation: Primer párrafo.

questions.stem: Why can competing microbes not survive?
options: The acids lower the pH too far.
questions.explanation: Segundo párrafo, explícito.

questions.stem: The word «diverge» in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Los cultivos se van diferenciando entre cocinas.

questions.stem: According to the passage, a mature starter is best described as
questions.explanation: «not a single culture but an ecosystem».

questions.stem: What do controlled studies suggest is the main cause of change?
questions.explanation: Último párrafo: lo atribuyen sobre todo a la harina.

questions.stem: The phrase «somewhat overstated» suggests the author considers the idea of local air
questions.explanation: «Somewhat» matiza: exagerada, no falsa del todo.

questions.stem: The word «tolerates» in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Soporta esas condiciones mejor que sus rivales.

questions.stem: What do the bacteria receive from the yeasts?
questions.explanation: «the yeasts release compounds that the bacteria use for growth».

questions.stem: It can be inferred that two starters kept in different homes will
questions.explanation: Divergen en semanas.

parts.title: Texto 2
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The construction of the first underground railways posed a problem that had no precedent: how to move large numbers of people through tunnels without suffocating them. Early lines used steam locomotives, and contemporary accounts describe conditions that would now be considered intolerable. Passengers emerged coated in soot, and the companies advertised the smoke as beneficial to the lungs, a claim that appears to have been believed by some.

Ventilation shafts were the first response. They were effective only near the openings, and cutting them through built-up areas was expensive and unpopular with the property owners above.

Electrification solved the problem, but not immediately and not because anyone anticipated it would. The early electric lines were built deep, using tunnelling shields, because deep tunnels avoided the cost of buying property along the route. Electric traction was adopted because steam was impossible at that depth, not because of the air quality at platform level.

The improvement in conditions was therefore a by-product of a decision made on financial grounds. This pattern recurs in the history of urban infrastructure often enough that some historians treat it as the norm rather than the exception: the stated reason for a change and the reason it actually occurred are frequently different, and the benefit that is remembered was rarely the one that was intended.

questions.stem: What problem did the first underground railways face?
questions.explanation: Primera frase.

questions.stem: How did companies describe the smoke?
questions.explanation: Lo dice explícitamente el primer párrafo.

questions.stem: Why were ventilation shafts unsatisfactory?
options: They were effective only near the openings.
questions.explanation: Segundo párrafo.

questions.stem: Why were the early electric lines built deep?
options: To avoid the cost of buying property.
questions.explanation: Razón económica, explícita.

questions.stem: Why was electric traction adopted?
options: Because steam was impossible at that depth.
Because it was cheaper than steam.
questions.explanation: Tercer párrafo, literal.

questions.stem: The word «by-product» in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Consecuencia no buscada.

questions.stem: What pattern do some historians treat as the norm?

parts.title: Texto 3
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Desert plants face a difficulty that has no obvious solution: the pores through which they take in carbon dioxide are the same pores through which they lose water. Opening them during the day, when light is available for photosynthesis, means losing water at the worst possible moment.

Several families of plants have arrived at the same answer independently. They open their pores at night, absorb carbon dioxide and store it chemically until daylight, when it is released internally and used. The pores stay shut all day.

The cost of this arrangement is speed. Storing and releasing carbon dioxide requires energy, and the amount that can be stored overnight limits how much photosynthesis is possible the following day. Plants using this pathway grow slowly, which is why it appears almost exclusively in environments where growing quickly is not an advantage.

Where water is abundant, these plants are outcompeted within a season. The trait is not a general improvement but a specialisation, and specialisations are expensive outside the conditions that produced them. This is a useful corrective to the habit of describing adaptations as though they were upgrades.

parts.passage:
The idea that a written constitution protects rights better than an unwritten one is widely held and difficult to demonstrate. Countries with detailed written guarantees have violated them; countries without a single codified document have maintained stable protections for centuries.

What appears to matter more than the document is whether an institution exists that can rule against the government and expect its ruling to be obeyed. That expectation is not created by writing it down. It accumulates through repeated instances in which a government complies with a decision it dislikes.

This suggests that constitutions describe a settlement rather than create one. Where the settlement is absent, the text is decorative; where it is present, the text records it and makes it harder to reverse quietly.

The practical implication is uncomfortable for reformers. A country that adopts an admirable constitution has not thereby acquired the habits the document assumes. Those habits are built slowly and can be destroyed quickly, and no clause has yet been drafted that prevents a government from simply ignoring it.

parts.title: Texto 5
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Volcanic eruptions are commonly ranked by the volume of material they eject, but for predicting their effect on climate that measure is misleading. What matters is how much sulphur reaches the stratosphere and how finely it is distributed there.

Sulphur dioxide converts into tiny droplets that reflect sunlight. If these remain in the lower atmosphere, rain removes them within days. If they reach the stratosphere, where there is no rain, they persist for a year or more and can lower global temperatures measurably.

This explains an apparent contradiction. The 1980 eruption of Mount St Helens ejected an enormous volume of rock but had almost no climatic effect, because the blast was lateral and little sulphur reached altitude. The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo ejected less material overall but sent sulphur far higher, and global temperatures fell by about half a degree over the following two years.

The practical consequence is that the eruptions worth monitoring for climate purposes are not necessarily the largest or the most destructive locally. A modest eruption at the right latitude, with the right sulphur content and sufficient vertical force, will affect more people than a spectacular one that does not reach the stratosphere.
